No result exists yet: the pass/fail depends on the platform run and on independent review.", "artifacts": [{"kind": "equivalence_report", "title": "Equivalence report: updown_counter.v (gold) vs updown_counter_refactor.v (gate)", "summary": "Serves [requirement:req-8077a859ef], which asks for an equivalence check of the existing up/down counter against its refactor. Gold is [artifact:prj-f735fc7be7.design-under-test.a1] updown_counter.v, which steps the count with an adder. Gate is [artifact:prj-f735fc7be7.design-under-test.a2] updown_counter_refactor.v, which steps the count with a bit-toggle chain. Both are approved, and their upstream review record is [evidence:prj-f735fc7be7.design-under-test.e1]. The setup equiv/updown_counter.eqy reads each file in its own [gold] or [gate] section and elaborates both with `prep -top updown_counter`. It names the same top and parameters, so the ports q, carry and borrow and the state register q line up by name. Proofs use only an `sby` strategy with the `smtbmc` engine at depth 16, which is the 4-bit state space. Per the knowledge document, a `sat` strategy can pass a wrong register partition, so `sat` is not listed and no weaker strategy follows. No result is reported here. The equivalence verdict, the partition count and the named gold and gate files will come only from the platform's equivalence.run over this setup. Reviewer action: re-run the setup against a mutant gate, such as a wrong reset value, a flipped carry condition or an off-by-one step. This confirms the setup actually observes those behaviours; the seat cannot do this itself because only one setup is submitted per run."}], "files": [{"path": "equiv/updown_counter.eqy", "kind": "equivalence_setup", "title": "eqy setup: updown_counter gold vs refactor gate", "summary": "Gold reads updown_counter.v [artifact:prj-f735fc7be7.design-under-test.a1] and gate reads updown_counter_refactor.v [artifact:prj-f735fc7be7.design-under-test.a2]. Each side runs prep -top updown_counter. The only strategy is sby with smtbmc at depth 16. It serves [requirement:req-8077a859ef].", "entry": "updown_counter"}], "tool_runs": [], "claims": ["By reading the two sources, the refactor looks equivalent at every output. When counting up, bit i toggles exactly when all lower bits are 1, which is an increment. When counting down, bit i toggles exactly when all lower bits are 0, which is a decrement. edge_hit (&same) equals q==15 when up and q==0 when down, so carry and borrow match gold. Reset and load priority are identical in both. This is a manual reading and has not been checked by any tool.", "The setup file is placed at equiv/updown_counter.eqy. It refers to the approved RTL as ../updown_counter.v and ../updown_counter_refactor.v. This assumes the platform places those files one directory above the setup, i.e. beside the equiv/ folder in the submission root. If the platform places them beside the setup file itself, the paths will not resolve and the run will be refused."], "escalation": null, "notes": "Exactly one equivalence_setup file is submitted, as equivalence.run requires. No file uses the approved RTL names. All commands come from the gate's allow list (read_verilog, prep). The [gold] and [gate] command lists differ because they read different files. All sections and strategy keys are on the gate's allow list. A placement risk is recorded in claims: if the approved RTL is placed directly beside the .eqy instead of one level up, the read paths should be changed to bare file names. The deliverable, equivalence_report, is the artifact above. The equivalence verdict will come from the platform's equivalence.run over equiv/updown_counter.eqy, and independent review is still required."}

=== FILE: equiv/updown_counter.eqy ===
[gold]
read_verilog ../updown_counter.v
prep -top updown_counter

[gate]
read_verilog ../updown_counter_refactor.v
prep -top updown_counter

[strategy sby]
use sby
depth 16
engine smtbmc
=== END FILE ===
